summary: A lively, popular Nimman restaurant for sampling Northern Thai/Lanna dishes family-style. Expect an open-air setting, crowds at dinner, and a broad menu rather than a quiet, formal meal.
whyGo: A straightforward first stop for shared Northern Thai staples such as nam prik dips, sai ua, hang lay curry, and larb kua.
Menu listings show many familiar dishes at roughly ฿60–150, making it practical to order several plates for a group.
bestFor: Groups wanting to try several regional dishes and sticky rice together.
Diners staying around Nimman who are comfortable with a busy, casual, open-air restaurant.
skipIf: You need a quiet or intimate dinner, dislike queues, or require a fully specified step-free route and accessible toilet.
You want a reliably vegan meal without checking ingredients: much of the signature menu uses meat, fish sauce, or shrimp paste.
duration: Plan about 60–90 minutes for a shared meal; this is a planning estimate, and a dinner queue may add time.
cost: Wongnai lists the venue as ฿฿ (about ฿101–250 per person) and current member-menu examples include nam prik noom ฿63, larb moo kua ฿77, and hang lay ฿113. Budget roughly ฿150–350 per person for several shared dishes and rice, excluding drinks; group order and appetite change the total.
hours: Listings show daily opening from 08:00, with closing at either 22:30 (Wongnai) or 23:00 (other directory). Confirm close time directly near your visit; holiday hours may differ.
bestTime: For dinner, arrive before the early-evening rush (around 17:00–17:30) or later in the evening; a local directory reports it is busy by 18:00. Lunch or mid-afternoon should be calmer, though service periods and dishes can vary.
gettingThere: At 11 Nimmanhaemin Road Soi 13, opposite Hallo Dormtel. Use a map pin for Tong Tem Toh, then walk into Soi 13 from Nimmanhaemin Road; a songthaew or ride-hail to Nimman is the simplest approach from elsewhere in Chiang Mai. Confirm pickup/drop-off access during busy hours.
booking: No dependable online reservation method was confirmed. Treat it as walk-in and allow time to join the queue; recent directory and visitor reports describe a numbered waiting system. Call +66 53 894 701 to check group seating or current booking practice.
accessibility: Tripadvisor lists wheelchair accessibility and outdoor seating, but no details about step-free entrance, ground surface, accessible toilet, or table spacing were verified. Contact the restaurant before relying on access accommodations.
practicalTips: Order several dishes to share: the listing's popular picks include pork larb kua, hang lay curry, nam prik noom, sai ua, and crispy pork belly.
Ask staff to reduce chilli if needed; this cuisine can be hot, and specify allergies clearly. Cross-contact and ingredient substitutions are not documented.
Vegetarian-friendly and vegan options are listed by Tripadvisor, but verify that fish sauce, shrimp paste, and meat stock can be omitted.
decemberNotes: December is within Chiang Mai's busy cool-season travel period; reserve extra time for dinner queues and check opening hours shortly before your date. No special December 2026 event or holiday schedule was confirmed.
uncertainties: Published closing times conflict (22:30 versus 23:00); holiday and December 2026 hours are not confirmed.
The restaurant's live menu and prices may change before December 2026; listed dish prices come from recently updated user menu entries.
Wheelchair accessibility is listed, but practical access details are unavailable; reservation rules and dietary handling also need direct confirmation.
